item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02010-1 This Review covers recent advances in quantum dots and perovskite nano-LEDs, discusses the challenge of balancing efficiency, stability and full-colour integration, and highlights potential future applications.

item.title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
item.description: arXiv:2610.30757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. item.title: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2610.31452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane.

item.title: Normally forbidden emissions from graphene could expose quantum fluctuations in incoming light
item.description: Voltage fluctuations, light fluctuations, temperature fluctuations—any fluctuations are troublesome and thus undesirable. They don't just cause discomfort; in engineering and medical applications, they affect the accuracy of measurements or introduce errors in controls. Even at the minute level of quantum phenomena, fluctuations are considered undesirable.

item.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
item.description: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂.

item.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
item.description: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws. The method could help speed up the search for new kinds of electronics and optical technologies, and contribute to more reliable quantum devices.

item.title: Perovskite chiral multiple quantum wells with extended spin lifetime via efficient spin cascade
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02027-6 Chiral multiple quantum wells enhance spin coherence in perovskites through spin cascade, achieving over 5-ns spin lifetime at room temperature.

item.title: Quantum probability can't be derived without assuming it first
item.description: For nearly a century, physicists have relied on the Born rule to calculate the chances of different outcomes when they measure a quantum system. Yet despite decades of effort, nobody has managed to derive the rule from more basic mathematical principles without making assumptions about probability along the way.
